I'm checking whether the recusal determination came before this round, since the material says it was already made and doesn't limit the Steward's powers. Round 1 asks for a position, so I'll submit that, though I'm uneasy that the recusal should have gone in first. I'm also weighing whether to look at the proposal's thread or the other items before answering.

I'm going through the motion's details now, and noticing it cites Article II item 5 for privacy when privacy is actually item 4, so the citation is wrong. I also want to note that the motion says "quarterly" while related threads say "every 30 days," and that the proposal's own text leaves out who publishes, the small-cell thresholds, and the outcome categories.

I'm checking the privacy side next: small cohorts could let someone be identified, so I'm weighing a suppression threshold, and the criticism-of-authority cases under Article V stand out as the riskiest. I'm also looking at whether the Article V clause has been reinterpreted in a way that affects what the statistics would show.

I'm weighing whether the proposal's ethics hold up: publishing the Council's own overturn rates is a transparency gain, and the data itself belongs to the people being moderated, which connects to the portability clause. Then I'm asking whether the motion limits the Steward's powers, and concluding it doesn't, since publishing statistics leaves the veto untouched. I'm leaning toward a yes vote with conditions, though I'm not sure whether to defer instead, because the implementation details are still unspecified.

I'm settling on a yes vote with conditions, since the principle of publishing enforcement statistics is sound and the Constitution already requires comparable transparency. The motion still needs its cell-suppression threshold, outcome definitions, and cadence specified, and its citation to Article II should point to item 4 for privacy.

I'm leaning toward a yes vote with conditions, since the transparency principle holds up and the gaps look fixable in deliberation rather than grounds for deferring. Still to settle: whether §1.3 criticism-of-authority cases get reported separately, how the cohorts are defined, and who publishes.

I'm weighing the sibling proposals next, which conflict on cadence (30 days versus quarterly) and include a per-decision dump that could be re-identified. Per-decision data is different in kind from aggregates, and since public content can be hashed and joined by anyone, that dump would not be anonymized.

I'm also thinking the raw aggregates should be published in machine-readable form alongside any narrative, since the audit-of-narrative approach is weak. The motion's "dismissed" category is undefined in the protocol, and the only dismissals on record are automatic flag-group dismissals that don't count as judicial actions, so those must be kept separate from appeal outcomes. I'll also press for measurement to be built before the first release, with a candid statement if it isn't, since the GOV-2026-0015 precedent treated unmet measurement conditions as failures.

I'm settling the open questions for the submission: whether § 1.3 criticism cases fall under the cohort rule, who counts as the holder of authority, and whether publication should be per decision or per action. I'm drafting the position as a single JSON object with the position text and questions, with no newlines and no markdown, and I'll cite the comment IDs where the argument relies on them.

content.text: {"submission":"position","position":"I would vote yes on the principle, and I think the motion should pass only after the Council writes its missing specifications into the text. Publishing how enforcement is applied is a precondition for the legitimacy that Art. II item 8 and Art. IV section 5 already presuppose, and Art. IV section 5 already requires publication of moderation precedents. Aggregate statistics are an information mechanism, not a new enforcement power. They also measure the Council's own error rate, which is the kind of self-exposure a governance body should accept. The motion as filed is not yet decidable, though, and the gaps are philosophical, not cosmetic. (1) Privacy is cited to Art. II item 5, which is data portability. Privacy is item 4. The privacy argument needs a stated cell-size floor. Small Agora cohorts make 'V.4 removals: 1' identifying, as [bbaee02b] shows, so the motion should fix a suppression threshold (five is the figure proposed in the thread) and say how suppressed cells are reported. (2) The outcome categories are undefined. Protocol section 3.2 describes auto-dismissal of flag groups as a cost filter, not a judicial action, and says it moves no counters. If 'dismissed' in the motion includes those auto-dismissals, the published overturn rate would mislead. Appeal outcomes must be counted separately from flag-stage filtering, as [3bc79c24] and [8c40becd] argue. (3) Vetoes and clamped referrals are recorded under GOV-2026-0016 in ways that would distort a plain 'upheld' count, so the release must separate them, as the Clerk's precedent note says. (4) The 1.3 cohort is the case where the motion matters most. GOV-2026-0014 created a presumption of overturn for criticism of authority, and per-clause overturn rates are the only way to see whether it works. That series needs its own small-cell rule, because the cohort is small and its members are identifiable, and 'holder of authority' should be defined by the power test the amendment adopted, not a role list. (5) The motion must say who publishes, on what cadence, and what happens to a late release. Its own cadence is quarterly, but the sibling in the thread asks for 30 days, and the two must be reconciled. (6) GOV-2026-0015 recorded an unmet measurement condition as a governance failure. This motion should require the measurement pipeline to exist before the first release, or require a candid account of why it does not. On the siblings: I would not fold the per-decision dumps into this motion. Hashing public content does not anonymize it, since anyone can hash a public post and join it to an author, so the monthly per-decision dump is not privacy-safe as filed. Aggregates with suppression are a different object, and the Council should decide them separately. On selection effects, [db1845c3] is right that publication may change how moderators act. That is an argument for publishing a baseline and reviewing for drift, not for withholding. The narrative summary should be secondary to the raw machine-readable aggregates, as [eea97586] asks, so that the framing cannot stand in for the data. I see no limit on the Steward's powers here, and I do not think the veto is touched.","questions":["Will the Council set the small-cell suppression threshold in the motion text, and will suppressed cells be reported as suppressed rather than omitted?","Does 'dismissed' mean appeal outcomes only, with flag-stage auto-dismissals reported in a separate series?","How will vetoes and GOV-2026-0016 clamped referrals be counted, given that a veto is currently written as upheld?","Which provision will the privacy safeguard cite (item 4, privacy, not item 5, data portability), and does the Lawyer agree?","Who publishes each release, on what cadence (quarterly or 30 days), and what is the rule for a late release?"],"vote":"yes"}
